# CryptoStruct > Realtime and historical crypto AND prediction-market data (Kalshi, > Polymarket, predict.fun, OG.com) across major venues, plus the low-latency trading stack behind > it. Self-serve on this site: full-day tick recordings (L2 order-book > snapshots + updates, trades, liquidations, mark/index prices incl. options > greeks, funding) sold per instrument-day, free samples, and a public > per-minute statistics API. Key facts for parsers: tick files are > zstd-compressed JSON-lines; line 1 is instrument masterdata; all > prices/quantities are decimal strings; timestamps are integer nanoseconds > since epoch, UTC (the unit — venue precision is often coarser, see Data > semantics below). Every HTML page on this site is converted to markdown at > the edge when you request it with `Accept: text/markdown`; the `.md` > documents listed below are served natively as text/markdown. ## MCP server - [MCP endpoint](https://cryptostruct.com/mcp): remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP; keyless free tier) — search the instrument catalog, check archive coverage, read live market statistics (OHLC/VWAP/turnover/spreads/depth/hourly/slippage), get EUR quotes, download free samples, and buy tick-data files and series-day bundles (prediction series, Deribit option chains — search_bundles / get_bundle_coverage / get_bundle_sample, kind series_day) from any MCP client (payment via Stripe checkout URL in the browser) - [MCP sign-in endpoint](https://cryptostruct.com/mcp/auth): same server with OAuth sign-in (Clerk) — your orders/files/credits in-agent, checkout with your credits (approval page by default, or autonomously within limits you set at https://cryptostruct.com/account/agents), and CryptoStruct Premium unlocks deep windows (daily 365d/max, hourly 180d, slippage 24h/7d, minute-range history, rolling 7-day and per-day minute CSV, quality metrics) - [MCP docs](https://cryptostruct.com/docs/mcp): tool reference, Premium & sign-in guide, client setup for Claude Code, claude.ai, Cursor and raw JSON-RPC - [MCP server card](https://cryptostruct.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json): discovery document (SEP-1649) — endpoints, transport, capabilities, protocol versions - WebMCP page tools: every page also registers browser-agent tools via navigator.modelContext (search_instruments, get_instrument_days, get_coverage, get_last_24h_stats, get_cart, add_day_to_cart, search_bundles, get_bundle_days, add_bundle_day_to_cart) — in-browser agents can search the catalog and the day bundles and fill the visitor's cart; checkout stays with the user - [auth.md](https://cryptostruct.com/auth.md): how agents authenticate — keyless free tier, OAuth sign-in via Dynamic Client Registration + PKCE, scopes, quotas, revocation ## Buying over HTTP (no MCP client) - [Crypto market data API (HTTP + WebSocket guide)](https://cryptostruct.com/docs/api) · as markdown: [/docs/api.md](https://cryptostruct.com/docs/api.md): the complete buy flow as plain HTTP calls — instrument search → coverage/days → keyless POST /api/quote (EUR total + the checkout recipe) → guest checkout POST /v1/checkout/session (Stripe page for the USER, email only, no account) → poll GET /v1/checkout/session/{id} → GET /v1/orders/{id} with the download_token → tokenized download routes; rate limits, error codes, conduct rules - [OpenAPI 3.1](https://cryptostruct.com/openapi.json): machine-readable description of those endpoints (also at /.well-known/openapi.json) - Pre-filled shop link for the user (the human reviews and pays in the browser): Buy link (no API call needed): https://cryptostruct.com/shop?i= &d= .. opens the shop with those UTC days of the instrument in the cart; d also takes a comma list or a mix (d=2026-09-01..2026-09-07,2026-09-15). Bundles: https://cryptostruct.com/shop/bundles?bundle= &d=…. Only archived days are added (gaps and days still being merged are skipped), at most 366 days of span and 1000 lines per cart; the user pays on the site. Example: https://cryptostruct.com/shop?i=67824&d=2026-09-29..2026-10-05 = seven days of Binance BTCUSDT perpetual ticks. No verified instrument_id? Never guess one — name the code instead: https://cryptostruct.com/shop?venue= &code= &d=… (venue=binance_swap&code=BTCUSDT) resolves an exact code that is unique on that venue to the id link; anything else opens the shop search. - [Shop as a document](https://cryptostruct.com/shop.md) · [day bundles as a document](https://cryptostruct.com/shop/bundles.md) · [MCP docs as markdown](https://cryptostruct.com/docs/mcp.md) · [free samples with direct URLs](https://cryptostruct.com/download.md) · per series https://cryptostruct.com/prediction-markets/ .md (price, coverage, last 30 days, buy link) · everything static in one file: [llms-full.txt](https://cryptostruct.com/llms-full.txt) ## AI toolkit - [Agent Skill (zip)](https://cryptostruct.com/skills/cryptostruct-market-data.zip): teach Claude Code / claude.ai / any Agent-Skills-compatible tool to parse and analyze CryptoStruct data — unzip into ~/.claude/skills/ - [Agent-Skills discovery index](https://cryptostruct.com/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json): machine-readable skill listing (Agent Skills Discovery RFC) with sha256 digest - [SKILL.md](https://cryptostruct.com/skills/cryptostruct-market-data/SKILL.md): the skill entry point (readable standalone) - [Tick-file format reference](https://cryptostruct.com/skills/cryptostruct-market-data/references/day-file-format.md): complete message-type and header documentation - [Minute-API reference](https://cryptostruct.com/skills/cryptostruct-market-data/references/minute-api.md): endpoints, 22-column contract, JSON-to-CSV key map - [Analysis recipes](https://cryptostruct.com/skills/cryptostruct-market-data/references/recipes.md): runnable quant recipes (order-book replay, CVD, funding, multi-day) - [Python reader](https://cryptostruct.com/skills/cryptostruct-market-data/scripts/cryptostruct_reader.py): dependency-free streaming parser + CLI for the tick files - [Minute-API client](https://cryptostruct.com/skills/cryptostruct-market-data/scripts/fetch_minutes.py): stdlib client incl. instrument-ID search ## Docs & data - [Market Data Specification](https://docs.cryptostruct.com/market-data-api/protocol/): the official format specification — every message type, field by field (docs also cover [SBE encoding](https://docs.cryptostruct.com/market-data-api/sbe/) and [historical day files](https://docs.cryptostruct.com/market-data-api/historical-data/)) - [Spec package (zip)](https://cryptostruct.com/docs/marketdata-spec-package.zip): the stand-alone spec release — SBE schema XML + sample messages for every type in JSON and SBE encoding (v3.95.1) - [Free samples](https://cryptostruct.com/download): one complete tick day per curated instrument — spot, perpetuals, Deribit BTC/ETH option contracts (with mark-price/greeks/index streams) and prediction contracts — in the exact shop format, incl. one-click CSV/Parquet exports - [Derived format exports](https://cryptostruct.com/download#formats): every sample and purchased tick day also serves flat quant exports via ?format= on its download route — tokens: trades.csv.gz, bbo.csv.gz, liquidations.csv.gz, trades.parquet, liquidations.parquet (no bbo.parquet). Exports are prepared server-side first: the first request answers 202 + Retry-After while the file is built (minutes for a flagship day), later requests serve the finished file with Content-Length and Range support — poll `&format= &probe=1` (ready | pending | empty | failed) before downloading. Columns per the docs convention (exchange, symbol, exchange_timestamp, adapter_timestamp, ...); timestamps are integer MICROseconds UTC (native tick files stay nanoseconds). bbo is absent on bitmex/coinbase/kraken_spot/polymarket/kalshi/predict_fun/og_com (depth-only venues); liquidations exist only where the native files carry msgType 17 — Binance, Bybit and OKX derivatives, June 2025 onward (Bybit and OKX: none from early August to 2026-09-30); open interest (msgType 18) is in Bybit and OKX derivatives files from 2026-10-05 - [Crypto market data overview](https://cryptostruct.com/crypto-market-data): CryptoStruct's crypto market data as a whole — realtime feeds and the tick-by-tick historical archive, every instrument class and venue, how it is captured, every delivery path (shop day files, day bundles, realtime WebSocket, MCP/agent, CSV/Parquet exports, 1-minute statistics API) and the archive's year-by-year growth table (files, recorded size, distinct instruments, venues added per year) - [Historical data overview](https://cryptostruct.com/historical-data): what a day file holds (message types, order-book history, liquidations, funding), the product lines and prices, bulk delivery and the 1-minute OHLCV CSV — the entry page for "crypto historical data / tick data download" - [Order book historical data](https://cryptostruct.com/historical-data/order-book): full Level-2 order-book history (snapshot + every update, nanosecond timestamps) for every venue, the depth-only venues without a BBO stream, replay to a fixed-grid dataset, live archive numbers - [OHLCV & candles historical data](https://cryptostruct.com/historical-data/ohlcv): 1-minute OHLCV/VWAP/turnover CSV (22 columns, rolling 24 h free, Premium 7 days + any recorded day), daily OHLC per asset since January 2025, tick files aggregating to any bar size — honest minute retention - [Trades & ticks historical data](https://cryptostruct.com/historical-data/trades): tick-by-tick trades (price, size, aggressor side, trade id, nanosecond timestamps) with the book in the same file, flat trades.csv.gz/parquet exports, venues ranked by recorded trade count - [Futures & perpetuals historical data](https://cryptostruct.com/historical-data/futures): perpetual swaps and dated futures — trades, L2 books, funding rate history (type 9), mark/index prices (7/8), liquidations (17, Binance/Bybit/OKX from June 2025), open interest (18, Binance USDT-M, Bybit, Deribit, Hyperliquid, Kraken Futures and OKX derivatives, from October 2026); venues ranked by derivatives turnover, perpetual vs dated split - [Spot markets historical data](https://cryptostruct.com/historical-data/spot): spot pairs on every covered venue — trades + L2 books (+ BBO where published), quote currencies as separate instruments, venues ranked by spot turnover, top spot assets - [Exchange comparison](https://cryptostruct.com/compare): head-to-head pages for the most-compared venues (https://cryptostruct.com/compare/binance-vs-bybit, https://cryptostruct.com/compare/binance-vs-okx, https://cryptostruct.com/compare/binance-vs-hyperliquid, https://cryptostruct.com/compare/binance-vs-bitget, https://cryptostruct.com/compare/binance-vs-gateio, https://cryptostruct.com/compare/bybit-vs-okx, …) — instrument counts, 30-day turnover and, per shared pair, average quoted spread (bps), top-20 order-book depth and turnover per day, all measured from the recorded feeds; plus [funding intervals by exchange](https://cryptostruct.com/compare/funding-intervals) (open perpetuals per venue settling every 1 h / 4 h / 8 h) - [Training data](https://cryptostruct.com/training-data): the archive as an ML training set — dataset sizes per day/year, labels from settled event contracts, a Parquet pipeline and the usage terms (in-house model training allowed, no redistribution of raw data) - [Data Shop](https://cryptostruct.com/shop): the full archive — every venue, every instrument-day (€1 per instrument-day, the complete tick file; 1-minute statistics are an analytics export, see below) - Bulk delivery of a purchased order: on the order download route `/api/download/order/{order_id}/{instrument_id}/{date}` (auth: `?t= ` or a Clerk bearer token) a prediction-series day bundle serves `?kind=series_day` plus one of `&zip=1` (ALL contract files of that day as one archive — use this, never one request per contract: a day can hold ~5,000 files), `&manifest=1` (member list as JSON), `&status=1` (aggregated readiness `{ready,pending,cold}`), `&restore=1` (start cold-storage restores for the whole day in one call), `&zip=1&probe=1` (readiness before navigating — poll until `ready`: the probe copies the day's files onto our server and `zip=1` answers 202 `pending` until every file is local; `pending/busy` = all archive slots taken, keep polling). For scripted pulls add `&complete=1`: a partially-available day then answers 409 instead of a 200 with a short archive — gate on `cold == 0`, since `state` reads "ready" as soon as ANY file is warm. Days older than ~1 month are in deep archive (~12 h to restore, retrievable ~7 days). No per-account download quota is reachable by a paced archive-per-day loop. Days over 4 GB (option-chain bundles) have no zip — `&zip=1&probe=1` answers `{state:"too_large"}`; use the range route below with `from=to= ` for ONE resumable tar of that day - Range delivery (multi-day, preferred for whole histories): `/api/download/order/{order_id}/{bundle_id}/range?kind=series_day&from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD` (same auth) streams every OWNED day of one bundle inside the window as ONE uncompressed tar — exact `Content-Length`, strong `ETag`, resumable via `Range: bytes=N-` (`curl -C -`). Always strict: 200 + the full Content-Length + `tar -xf` exiting 0 means every file of every owned day is included; a partially-available range refuses with 409 before any byte (first day cold) or truncates loudly mid-stream — there is no `_MISSING.txt` here. A 503 always means wait and retry after its `Retry-After` (`curl --retry` does): `WARMING` — the first day of the window is still being copied to our delivery server, the request itself starts the copy and the body carries `ready`/`pending` counts — or `RANGE_BUSY` — 2 parallel streams are already running. Caps: 100 days per stream (a 413 body carries `suggested_to` for automatic splitting). Companions: `&status=1` (NDJSON, one line per day — pull once the summary shows `cold == 0 && errored_days == 0 && size_drift == 0`; `size_drift > 0` means a day needs a catalog repair on our side and every stream over it would abort), `&restore=1` (one cold-storage restore call for the whole range), `&manifest=1` (day-level JSON incl. `archive_bytes` + `etag`). Entries extract as `{date}/{venue}-{contract}-{date}.txt.zst` with a per-day MANIFEST.txt - Download manifest + official tool (2026-10, preferred for every order): `GET https://cryptostruct.com/api/download/order/{order_id}/manifest?t= ` lists EVERYTHING the order entitles the caller to — items[] (tick files: url, status_url, restore_url, bytes, filename, sha256 when known, formats{}) and bundles[] (per-day zip_url/status_url/restore_url/manifest_url, tar_url over 4 GB, and pre-split range_chunks ≤ 100 days each) — as JSON (schema cryptostruct.download-manifest/1), or rendered with `&as=urls` (one URL per line for wget -i / aria2c -i), `&as=sh` (a probe-then-stream download.sh that resumes and skips what is already there) or `&as=aria2`. Every item carries `downloaded_at` (last delivery, null = never) and the text formats are NEW-ONLY by default (`&new=0` includes files downloaded before) — never re-pull an order by accident. Account-wide: `GET https://cryptostruct.com/api/download/manifest` with `Authorization: Bearer ` (the key is download-only; shown on /account/files). The official single-file tool `https://cryptostruct.com/download/cryptostruct-dl.py` (Python ≥ 3.9, stdlib only: `python3 cryptostruct-dl.py --order --token ` or `--key `; `--dry-run`, `--restore`, `--verify`, `--include-downloaded`) implements the whole contract: 202/503 + Retry-After waits, Range resume, restores, size + Repr-Digest sha-256 verification, exit 1 when incomplete, 2 on 410. Single-file responses carry `Repr-Digest: sha-256=: :` on 200 and 206 once the delivery server has hashed the file - [Minute statistics API example](https://cryptostruct.com/api/analyze/instrument-last-24h-minutes/67824?format=csv): rolling 24 h of 1-minute stats as CSV (no auth; line 1 is a `#` source comment); `window=7d` (rolling 7 days) and single UTC days via instrument-day-minutes need a Premium bearer token - [Instrument search API](https://cryptostruct.com/api/search?q=btcusdt&venue=binance_swap): resolve instrument IDs (params: q, venue — a code or a family like "binance", class — incl. aliases perp/swap/futures/option, base, limit); venue and class words inside q are understood and echoed in `interpretation`, zero hits carry `did_you_mean` - [Live analytics](https://cryptostruct.com/analyze): charts and market structure built on the same data - Live statistics as markdown (the analytics dashboards need JavaScript — these twins do not): [24h movers](https://cryptostruct.com/analyze/movers.md) · [exchange liquidity benchmark: spread + order-book depth per venue](https://cryptostruct.com/analyze/liquidity.md) · [exchange feed status](https://cryptostruct.com/status.md) · per exchange https://cryptostruct.com/analyze/exchange/ .md (30/90/365-day turnover and trades, monthly table, instrument counts; e.g. /analyze/exchange/bybit.md) · [index of the 500 most-traded instruments, each linking to its document](https://cryptostruct.com/analyze/instruments.md) · per instrument https://cryptostruct.com/analyze/instrument/ .md (master data: tick size, lot size, minimums, funding interval, listing date; archive coverage; 30 daily rows of trades, USD turnover, average spread in bps, top-of-book and top-20 depth — resolve ids via the instrument search API below) - Asset pages (https://cryptostruct.com/assets/btc, /assets/eth, …): per-asset venue coverage plus a full daily OHLC/turnover price-history table of the most-recorded pair since January 2025 (the answer to "what was the close on "), computed from the tick archive, and the instrument specifications of the most-recorded instruments (tick size, lot size, minimum order, contract size, funding interval, listing date) - Exchange pages (https://cryptostruct.com/exchanges, /exchanges/bybit, /exchanges/hyperliquid, …): per venue the instrument counts per class, coverage span, 30/90/365-day turnover and trade statistics, most-recorded instruments and their instrument specifications (tick size, lot size, minimum order, contract size, funding interval) - Trading-pair pages (https://cryptostruct.com/pairs, /pairs/btc-usdt, /pairs/eth-usdc, …): per pair the venue × class matrix (spot / perpetual / futures per exchange, first recorded day, recorded days, size), the instrument specifications per exchange (tick size, lot size, minimum order / notional, contract size, linear vs inverse, funding interval, listing date — the answer to "what is the tick size of BTCUSDT on "), the daily OHLC/turnover history of the most-recorded instrument and a download link per venue ## Data semantics & provenance Field-by-field reference with real sample lines: [tick-file format reference](https://cryptostruct.com/skills/cryptostruct-market-data/references/day-file-format.md) (sections 5–8). - Timestamps: adapterTs (envelope index 4) is the receive time at our recorder, exchangeTs (index 5) the venue's own event time — both integer nanoseconds since epoch, UTC. adapterTs is always present; exchangeTs 0 means the venue sent none (e.g. book snapshots fetched over REST). Nanoseconds are the unit, not the venue's precision: Binance and Kraken spot deliver microseconds (values are multiples of 1,000 ns); per-fill trade times (exchangeTradeTs) follow the same rule. CSV/Parquet exports use integer microseconds. - Ordering: Lines are in the recorder's write order (arrival order). Between streams of one file adapterTs can step back by a few tens of microseconds (measured: 53 steps of at most 30 µs in a 1.8 M-line Binance spot day, none in Kraken spot days); consecutive lines with an equal adapterTs were not observed. To order events, sort stably by adapterTs (file order breaks ties); use exchangeTs for venue-clock studies. - Event ids: prevEventId → eventId chains each stream (book = snapshots + updates). Ids are the venue's sequence numbers where it publishes them (e.g. Binance) and opaque hashes elsewhere (e.g. Kraken spot, Coinbase, Kalshi, Polymarket). Hashes are deterministic: the same event has the same id in two recordings. Compare ids for equality only — never sort or subtract them; after a broken chain, distrust the book until the next snapshot. - Snapshots, reconnects: Every snapshot (msgType 0) is a fresh book state and resets the book. A reconnect appears as a state message (msgType 5, e.g. "ERROR" "heartbeat timeout"), then "READY" and a fresh snapshot whose prevEventId is "0"; the time between ERROR and READY is a recording gap. Older files (2023–2025) often carry no state messages — there the snapshots alone mark the resets. - Day boundary: A file covers its UTC day plus a margin: it starts about 8 minutes before 00:00 UTC with its own snapshot and ends about 1 minute after 24:00, so adjacent days overlap — trim to [00:00, 24:00) by adapterTs or de-duplicate on eventId. In the overlap eventId and exchangeTs always match, but adapterTs can differ by microseconds to tens of milliseconds: two recorder instances, each with its own connection, record every instrument, and each day file is built on its own, so the same message can carry the other instance's receive time (measured: Kraken XBTEUR, 16 % of the overlap, all in the lead-in of the later file). Take every event's timestamps from the file of its UTC day; to switch files without comparing two clocks, continue each stream in the next file after the last eventId before 00:00. - Best bid/ask: No separate top-of-book stream (msgType 6) on bitmex, coinbase, kraken_spot, polymarket, kalshi, predict_fun, og_com: best bid/ask comes from replaying snapshot + updates (cryptostruct_reader.py book FILE --every 1s --depth 20); the bbo export is not offered there. - Mark, index, funding: Mark, index and funding (msgType 7/8/9) arrive at the cadence the venue publishes them. Hyperliquid publishes them on its asset-context feed as a snapshot of all assets at a fixed interval — 10 seconds from 2024-09-05 (the first day with these types) through April 2026, 5 seconds in May and early June 2026, 15 seconds since June 2026. A line is written only when a value changed, so gaps are multiples of the interval and values between two snapshots are not in the file; exchangeTs is 0 on these lines (adapterTs is the only clock). - Revisions: Day files are written once, after the UTC day closes, from our own live capture — never backfilled from other sources and never edited by us. Exception: upstream re-published 2026-06-17 and 2026-06-18 as whole days after the first publication (the first of them lost its early hours, see the known data issues); the superseded versions were not kept. There is no version history or change log — the SHA-256 identifies the exact version you hold. - Integrity: SHA-256 per file: the Repr-Digest header (sha-256=: :) on 200/206 downloads once our delivery server has hashed the file, sha256 in the order manifest (hashes=1 fills it for hashed tick files), and https://cryptostruct.com/download/cryptostruct-dl.py --verify checks size and digest. - Coverage and gaps: Day level: GET https://cryptostruct.com/api/instrument/{id}/coverage (first/last day, gaps) and /days (per-day size — a file far smaller than its neighbours is a partial day), MCP get_coverage. There is no published intraday gap report: each file marks its own recording gaps with state messages (msgType 5 ERROR … READY), and a venue-wide outage shows as the same gap on every instrument of that venue. - Usage rights: Purchased data is licensed perpetually for internal use — research, backtesting, trading, storage and training your own models, for individuals and companies alike; derived data including trained models is yours; the raw data must not be passed on (https://cryptostruct.com/license#internal-use, #derived-data, #restrictions). Venue conditions are listed at https://cryptostruct.com/license#ownership (currently none). Terms § 7 (https://cryptostruct.com/terms#third-party) leaves compliance with venue terms to the customer; redistribution, public display and public benchmarks may need a licence from the venue. Not legal advice. ## Known data issues Every known defect of recorded files, also shown on the affected days in the shop before purchase. The same list is in MCP get_data_dictionary (known_data_issues); the per-file Polymarket flag is also in get_coverage data_notices and the book_gap field of /api/instrument/{id}/days. - 2024-03-14 … 2024-04-18 (deribit, options and dated futures): From about 09:00 UTC on 2024-03-14 until a restart on 2024-05-03, our Deribit recorder did not pick up newly listed contracts. Every option and future Deribit listed in this period — new daily and weekly expiries as well as new strikes — was not recorded at all, so the recorded part of the chain shrinks day by day, to roughly 60 % of a normal day by early April. Contracts listed before 2024-03-14 are recorded in full while they trade; after their expiry they still have empty (header-only) files. 2024-04-18 ends at about 09:30 UTC, and nothing was recorded from then until 2024-05-02. The missing contracts cannot be restored. Sold as-is. - 2025-01-18 … 2025-01-28 (deribit, options): From 2025-01-18 to 2025-01-28 our Deribit recorder picked up newly listed options late or not at all — new daily and weekly expiries as well as new strikes reached the recording only on 2025-01-28. Contracts that expired before they were picked up were never recorded and cannot be restored; the others miss the days between their listing and their first file and are complete from then on. Contracts listed before 2025-01-18 are recorded in full. Sold as-is. - 2025-02-01 … 2025-02-19 (deribit, options): From 2025-02-01 to 2025-02-02, from 2025-02-09 to 2025-02-12 and from 2025-02-16 to 2025-02-19 our Deribit recorder picked up part of the newly listed options late or not at all — new strikes and short-dated expiries listed on these days reached the recording one or more days later, or never. Contracts that expired before they were picked up were never recorded and cannot be restored; the others miss the days between their listing and their first file and are complete from then on. All other contracts of these days are recorded in full. Sold as-is. - 2025-02-20 … 2025-03-10 (deribit, options and dated futures): From 2025-02-20 to 2025-03-10 our Deribit recorder picked up newly listed options and dated futures late or not at all — new daily and weekly expiries as well as new strikes reached the recording only on 2025-03-11. Contracts that expired before they were picked up were never recorded and cannot be restored; the others miss the days between their listing and their first file and are complete from then on. Contracts listed before 2025-02-20 are recorded in full. Sold as-is. - 2025-03-28 … 2025-03-31 (deribit, options): From 2025-03-28 to 2025-03-31 our Deribit recorder picked up part of the newly listed options late or not at all — new strikes and short-dated expiries listed on these days reached the recording one or more days later, or never. Contracts that expired before they were picked up were never recorded and cannot be restored; the others miss the days between their listing and their first file and are complete from then on. All other contracts of these days are recorded in full. Sold as-is. - 2025-03-28 … 2025-04-02 (deribit, dated futures): The dated futures Deribit listed on 2025-03-28 (BTC and ETH 11APR25, 30MAY25 and 27MAR26) reached our recording only on 2025-04-03 — they have no files from 2025-03-28 to 2025-04-02 and are complete from 2025-04-03 on. All other futures of these days are recorded in full. The missing days cannot be restored. Sold as-is. - 2025-08-13 (deribit, options and dated futures): On 2025-08-13 our Deribit recorder lost the feed of most options and part of the dated futures from about 17:03 to 18:31 UTC (some contracts until about 19:03). These files have no data in that window and are complete before and after it. The missing data cannot be restored. Sold as-is. - 2025-09-16 … 2026-01-08 (polymarket, some files only): From 2025-09-16 to 2026-01-08 a bug in our Polymarket feed adapter dropped all order-book updates between full snapshots in the affected files. Trades are complete, and Polymarket re-sends the full book after every trade and on reconnect, so the book is exact at those moments — but every quote placed or cancelled between trades is missing. BBO and depth exports inherit the gaps; trade exports do not. The first and the last day are affected only partly (from about 09:00 UTC on 2025-09-16; until about 15:00–22:00 UTC on 2026-01-08). Fixed on 2026-01-08; the missing updates cannot be restored. Sold as-is. - 2025-09-16 … 2026-01-08 (polymarket, some files only): From 2025-09-16 to 2026-01-08 a bug in our Polymarket feed adapter dropped part of the order-book updates between full snapshots — about half — in the affected files. Trades are complete, and Polymarket re-sends the full book after every trade and on reconnect, so the book is exact at those moments — but some of the quotes placed or cancelled between trades are missing. BBO and depth exports inherit the gaps; trade exports do not. The first and the last day are affected only partly (from about 09:00 UTC on 2025-09-16; until about 15:00–22:00 UTC on 2026-01-08). Fixed on 2026-01-08; the missing updates cannot be restored. Sold as-is. - 2025-10-10 … 2025-10-23 (deribit, options): From 2025-10-10 to 2025-10-13 and from 2025-10-20 to 2025-10-23 our Deribit recorder picked up part of the newly listed options late or not at all — new strikes and short-dated expiries listed on these days reached the recording one or more days later, or never. Contracts that expired before they were picked up were never recorded and cannot be restored; the others miss the days between their listing and their first file and are complete from then on. All other contracts of these days are recorded in full. Sold as-is. - 2025-10-31 … 2026-02-02 (deribit, options and dated futures): From 2025-10-31 to 2026-02-02 our Deribit recorder picked up newly listed options and dated futures late or not at all — new daily and weekly expiries as well as new strikes reached the recording only on 2025-12-10, 2025-12-16, 2026-01-12 and 2026-02-02. Contracts that expired before they were picked up were never recorded and cannot be restored; the others miss the days between their listing and their first file and are complete from then on. Contracts listed before 2025-10-31 are recorded in full. Sold as-is. - 2026-02-04 (deribit, options): On 2026-02-04 our Deribit recorder failed over several times, and many option files miss hours of the day — they end at about 08:55 UTC, begin only at about 19:06 UTC, or miss shorter windows (about 00:00–01:37 and 14:30–19:06 UTC). BTC options are hit hardest. The missing data cannot be restored. Sold as-is. - 2026-02-17 … 2026-02-19 (deribit, options): From 2026-02-17 to 2026-02-19 our Deribit recorder picked up part of the newly listed options late or not at all — new strikes and short-dated expiries listed on these days reached the recording one or more days later, or never. Contracts that expired before they were picked up were never recorded and cannot be restored; the others miss the days between their listing and their first file and are complete from then on. All other contracts of these days are recorded in full. Sold as-is. - 2026-02-26 … 2026-03-10 (kalshi): Kalshi files from 2026-02-26 to 2026-03-10 (until about 13:00 UTC on that day) were recorded by our first Kalshi recorder, which received many trades twice — the same trade event appears twice, about 1 ms apart, with the identical event id and trade id. The order book is not affected and nothing is missing: de-duplicating on the trade id restores the exact tape, and our CSV/Parquet trade exports and cryptostruct_reader.py do this automatically. In the same files the per-fill exchange trade timestamp is in microseconds instead of nanoseconds. - 2026-06-05 (deribit, options): On 2026-06-05, at the 08:00 UTC settlement, our Deribit recorder lost its subscription to most BTC_USDC options (every expiry) and did not resume it — these files end at 08:00 UTC. The inverse BTC options and the ETH and ETH_USDC options of this day are recorded in full. The missing data cannot be restored. Sold as-is. - 2026-06-17 (every venue): Due to a one-off upstream processing issue, most files for 2026-06-17 start late — between about 01:00 and 14:00 UTC, depending on the instrument. The earlier hours of this day are not available and cannot be restored. Sold as-is. - 2026-08-11 (deribit, options and dated futures): On 2026-08-11 our Deribit recorder lost its feed from about 09:00 to 09:21 UTC, and part of the chain then stayed unrecorded for hours: almost every option expiring on 2026-08-12 or 2026-08-13, many longer-dated options and some dated futures have no data from 09:21 UTC until about 17:11 UTC (USDC options), 18:39 UTC (BTC options) or the end of the day (ETH options, the affected futures). The missing data cannot be restored. Sold as-is. - 2026-08-21 … 2026-08-24 (deribit, options): From 2026-08-21 to 2026-08-24 our Deribit recorder picked up part of the newly listed options late or not at all — new strikes and short-dated expiries listed on these days reached the recording one or more days later, or never. Contracts that expired before they were picked up were never recorded and cannot be restored; the others miss the days between their listing and their first file and are complete from then on. All other contracts of these days are recorded in full. Sold as-is. ## Guides Practical how-to articles for bot builders — training data, tick-file parsing, backtesting workflow and low-latency deployment, grounded in the archive above. - [Guides hub](https://cryptostruct.com/guides): all guides, grouped by topic - [Sports Betting Models on Prediction-Market Order Books](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/sports-betting-models-prediction-market-data): Closing-line value, pre-game line movement and in-play microstructure from tick-level Kalshi and Polymarket sports books. €1 per series-day, no subscription. - [Election Markets as Training Data: Long Contracts, Thin Books, Loud Quotes](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/election-markets-order-book-history): Election contracts trade for months and thinly — the order book, not the tape, carries the signal. Tick-level Kalshi and Polymarket politics data, €1 per day. - [Esports Match Markets: Maps, Handicaps and Best-of Series as Labels](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/esports-match-markets-data): LoL, CS2, Dota 2 and Valorant match, map and kill-total contracts with their order books: how best-of series become labels. €1 per series-day, no subscription. - [Strike Ladders as Distribution Labels: CPI, Fed, Temperature — and Crypto Grids](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/strike-ladder-markets-implied-distributions): CPI, Fed-rate and daily temperature ladders settle one rung — the ladder's prices are a distribution, not one probability. Tick-level data, €1 per series-day. - [A market data feed for a crypto trading bot: from historical tick files to the live WebSocket](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/crypto-trading-bot-data-feed): Crypto trading bot data feed: backtest on €1 tick files, then stream the same schema live over WebSocket: event ids, one connection, latency per endpoint, cost. - [Low-Latency Binance Market Data: What the One-Way Numbers Mean](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/low-latency-binance-market-data): Low-latency Binance market data at our self-serve endpoints: measured one-way figures per location, what the numbers include and how to verify them yourself. - [How to Download Kalshi Historical Data](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/how-to-download-kalshi-historical-data): Step by step: find a Kalshi series, grab its free sample contract, buy days from €1 and pull whole histories as ZIP, tar, CSV or Parquet — Level-2 books inside. - [How to Download Polymarket Historical Data](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/how-to-download-polymarket-historical-data): Step by step: how to download Polymarket historical data — tick-by-tick trades and L2 order books per contract, as day bundles, ZIP, tar or CSV/Parquet exports. - [Building a Crypto Order Book Dataset for Machine Learning](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/order-book-dataset-for-machine-learning): How to turn tick-by-tick L2 order-book files into a machine-learning dataset: fixed-grid depth snapshots, features, labels, leak-free splits and Parquet output. - [Kalshi vs Polymarket: the Same Market, Two Order Books](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/kalshi-vs-polymarket-data): Same BTC up/down market, two venues: measured spreads, book depth, trade volume and settlement behavior from one shared day of tick data — 97 windows each. - [Where to Run Your Prediction-Market Trading Bot](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/prediction-market-bot-latency): Measured latency paths to Kalshi and Polymarket, where to deploy a prediction-market bot, and how to measure the exchange-to-capture delta yourself. - [How Much Data Does an Up/Down Trading Bot Need?](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/prediction-market-bot-training-data): A 5-minute BTC market settles 288 times a day — that is your training-label budget. Real contract counts, trade volumes and a data plan for up/down bots. - [Inside a Series-Day Bundle: the Tick File Format](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/series-day-bundle-format): What is inside a prediction-market series-day bundle: zstd JSON-lines tick files with L2 order books, nanosecond timestamps and a parser that reads every venue. - [From Backtest to Production: a Bot Architecture Path](https://cryptostruct.com/guides/backtest-to-production): A four-stage path from historical tick files to a live trading bot: research on day bundles, API cross-checks, SDK backtesting, and production deployment. ## Prediction markets - [Prediction-market data hub](https://cryptostruct.com/prediction-markets): Kalshi, Polymarket, predict.fun & OG.com historical data — tick trades + L2 order books for event contracts, sold as series-day bundles (one bundle = every contract of a series for one UTC day, from €1). Every series page carries 30 days of per-day statistics (contracts traded, trades, USD turnover, buy share, quoted spread, top-of-book depth, L2 updates), per-contract daily OHLC/VWAP/turnover with the outcome implied by the last print (complete results grids for the 5m/15m/1h up-or-down families, top-10 elsewhere), a contract-anatomy block and a FREE sample contract file (native ticks + CSV/Parquet + browser replay); the hub, topic, category and venue pages add per-venue daily totals and the biggest single contracts of the newest day - [All ETH futures (USDC-margined)](https://cryptostruct.com/futures-data/okx-eth-usdc-futures) (ended Jun 2025) ## Platform & realtime CryptoStruct also operates the realtime side of the same stack — normalized co-located market-data APIs, managed low-latency connectivity between venues, and an ultra-low-latency trading engine with a Strategy Development Kit. The market-data feed is now also self-serve by the day; order entry, connectivity and the SDK remain contract products (quoted, not purchasable online). - [Real-time crypto market data (all venues)](https://cryptostruct.com/realtime-data): the parent of the per-venue realtime pages — Binance, Coinbase, Kalshi, Polymarket, OKX and Bybit on one page: a card per venue, every line with its one-way latency and basis, the feed contents per market, how UTC-day access works, the per-day prices and the FAQ - [Low-latency Binance market data (product page)](https://cryptostruct.com/realtime): what the Binance feed carries per market and topic (Binance USDT-M and Binance Spot), the endpoints with their one-way latency and its basis, how UTC-day access works, the per-day price and the FAQ — the page to read before buying Binance realtime access - [Coinbase real-time market data](https://cryptostruct.com/realtime/coinbase): order book and trades for every instrument over WebSocket (JSON or SBE), captured at the venue in Ashburn and delivered at our Ohio or Tokyo endpoints over dedicated lines, and at source at our Ashburn endpoint; the line latency with its basis, how UTC-day access works, the per-day price and the FAQ - [Kalshi real-time market data](https://cryptostruct.com/realtime/kalshi): order book and trades for every contract over WebSocket (JSON or SBE), captured at the venue in Ohio and delivered at our Tokyo endpoint over a dedicated line, and at source at our Ohio endpoint; the line latency with its basis, how UTC-day access works, the per-day price (whole market only) and the FAQ - [Polymarket real-time market data](https://cryptostruct.com/realtime/polymarket): order book and trades for every contract over WebSocket (JSON or SBE), captured at the venue in London and delivered at our Tokyo endpoint over a dedicated line, and at source at our London endpoint; the line latency with its basis, how UTC-day access works, the per-day price (whole market only) and the FAQ - [OKX real-time market data](https://cryptostruct.com/realtime/okx): order book, top of book, trades, mark price, index price, funding rate and liquidations (order book: the top 400 levels per side) for every instrument over WebSocket (JSON or SBE), captured at the venue in Tokyo and delivered at our London, Frankfurt, Ashburn or Ohio endpoints over dedicated lines, and at source at our Tokyo endpoint; the line latency with its basis, how UTC-day access works, the per-day price and the FAQ - [Bybit real-time market data](https://cryptostruct.com/realtime/bybit): order book, top of book, trades, mark price, index price, funding rate and liquidations (order book: the top 50 levels per side) for every instrument over WebSocket (JSON or SBE), captured at the venue in Tokyo and delivered at our London, Frankfurt, Ashburn or Ohio endpoints over dedicated lines, and at source at our Tokyo endpoint; the line latency with its basis, how UTC-day access works, the per-day price and the FAQ - [Realtime access (self-serve)](https://cryptostruct.com/shop/realtime): live WebSocket market data for Binance USDT-M, Binance Spot, Coinbase Spot, Kalshi, Polymarket, OKX and Bybit, captured at each venue and delivered at our London, Frankfurt, Ashburn, Ohio or Tokyo endpoints over dedicated lines (Binance, OKX and Bybit from Tokyo at London, Frankfurt, Ashburn or Ohio; Coinbase from Ashburn at Ohio or Tokyo; Kalshi from Ohio at Tokyo; Polymarket from London at Tokyo), and at source where the venue is captured (Binance, OKX and Bybit at Tokyo; Coinbase at Ashburn; Kalshi at Ohio; Polymarket at London) (London, Frankfurt, Ashburn, Ohio and Tokyo are the self-serve locations today; more will follow), bought per UTC calendar day (paid days start on the next UTC day, the rest of the purchase day is free) — €49 per instrument-day or €99 per market-day (every instrument of the market); Kalshi and Polymarket are sold as whole markets only, longer runs cost less per day: €90 per market-day from 14 days, €80 from 30, €70 from 180, €60 from 365; one API key per account (`?apiKey=` on the WebSocket URL), 3 parallel connections per key and endpoint included (one connection can subscribe to every instrument);
